html:
Bactria was the land between the Hindu Kush and the Oxus River, the Amu Darya, in what is now northern Afghanistan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan. The map shows it around 200 BCE as the Greco-Bactrian Kingdom, which then ruled far beyond Bactria itself.

Bactria was rich farmland and a crossroads of trade. It had been home to the Oxus Civilisation and was a province of the Achaemenid Empire. Alexander took it after hard fighting and settled Greek soldiers there. Under the Seleucid Empire it was governed by Diodotus, who broke away and made himself king around 250 BCE.

The Greek kings of Bactria built cities such as Ai-Khanoum and struck fine coins. Around 180 BCE they pushed south into India, starting the line of Indo-Greek kings. Nomads ended the kingdom around 130 BCE, when Saka and then the Yuezhi overran it. The Yuezhi later founded the Kushan Empire here.
